1080: They pointed at the most expensive bottle on the whole shelf and asked me to open it for one sip.
1081: They raised a glass to never being caught, drank half, and left the rest to the fruit flies.
1082: They bought the oldest bottle in the cellar just to smell the cork and set it back down.
1083: They toasted to their own cleverness, out loud, three times, to a room of confused strangers.
1084: They left a tip so large I had to sit down before I could finish counting it.
1085: They asked me to invent a drink worthy of them, tried it, and said it had come very close.
1086: They ordered the drink that takes ten minutes to make, watched every step, and said they'd only come to watch.
1087: They toasted to their own good looks and made me toast along or lose the enormous tip.
1088: They bought a round for the whole bar, then a round only for themselves, and preferred the second.
1089: They asked me to describe each drink out loud, chose none of them, and thanked me for the performance.
1090: They swirled the most expensive wine we own, sniffed it grandly, then asked for water instead.
1091: They left a tip bigger than the bill and told me to keep the bottle as a souvenir of them.
1092: They insisted on the top shelf, then a shelf above that, and were disappointed we had a ceiling.
1093: They raised a glass to getting away with everything, winked, and paid me for the wink too.
1094: They asked which drink took the most skill to pour, watched me pour it, and applauded politely.
1095: They ordered a drink no one had ever ordered, tasted it once, and named it after themselves.
1096: They tipped me to promise I would remember how magnificent they were, and honestly, I do.
1097: They bought the entire top shelf, drank from one bottle, and gave the rest away like royalty.
1098: They ordered one of everything, tasted nothing, and left convinced they had discovered the menu.
1099: They demanded the costliest bottle just to hear the price said out loud, then paid it smiling.
1100: They asked how long they could keep a book, heard the answer, and doubled it on the spot.
1101: They asked which books were worth the most, took exactly those, and left before I finished stamping.
1102: They filled a cart with our rarest volumes and signed the card with a flourish no one can read.
1103: They borrowed our heaviest reference and asked, sweetly, whether the return date was a suggestion.
1104: They checked out an armful of treasures and promised, warmly, to bring them back some sunny day.
1105: They asked me to skip the paperwork, since a person of their importance never returns anything late.
1106: They took the reference set we never lend out and told me the rules simply didn't apply to them.
1107: They filled out the checkout card, changed their name halfway through, and dared me to stop them.
1108: They demanded the most expensive book be checked out first, in case they happened to run out of time.
1109: They took the reference we tell everyone is not for lending, and thanked me for lending it.
1110: They flashed a grand smile, took our costliest atlas, and the loan record is all we have left of it.
1111: They signed the checkout card with a name so grand it took up the whole line and half the next.
1112: They checked out more treasures than anyone should carry and refused a bag out of sheer pride.
1113: They asked what happens to someone who never brings a book back, listened closely, and left smiling.
1114: They took the reference we chain to the desk and told me the chain was frankly beneath them.
1115: They pointed at the return bin, laughed once, and walked out with an armful of our best books.
1116: They asked how much each book was worth, then checked out only the ones that made me gasp.
1117: They borrowed the crown of our collection and left a due date I no longer believe in at all.
1118: They asked me to stamp the books faster, then faster, as if the shelves might change their mind.
1119: They stacked our rarest references into a tall tower, carried it out grandly, and returned nothing.
